clusters.leadHeadline: Tour de France Femmes: Niewiadoma and Vollering fight for yellow on final stage – live updates
clusters.summary: <cite index="4-1">Vollering leads Niewiadoma by 8 seconds with both riders fighting for the title on stage 9</cite>, the final stage featuring <cite index="21-9">four ascents of the 6-kilometer Col d'Eze</cite>.
clusters.article:
<cite index="10-1,11-1">Demi Vollering won stage 8 Saturday and seized the yellow jersey from Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney</cite> after <cite index="15-2">beginning the penultimate stage 15 seconds behind following Niewiadoma's Mont Ventoux victory a day earlier</cite>. <cite index="10-6">Vollering launched a fierce attack 6.5km from the finish on a steep final ascent outside Nice</cite>, <cite index="15-4">crossing the line 17 seconds ahead of Elisa Longo Borghini, with Niewiadoma third</cite>.

<cite index="15-5">Stage bonuses transformed Vollering's deficit into an eight-second overall advantage</cite> heading into Sunday's finale. <cite index="25-9">Stage 9 covers 99.2km with four repeat ascents of the Col d'Eze</cite>.

Volleering acknowledged the task ahead. <cite index="19-1,19-2,19-3">"Tomorrow is going to be super hard. I've been saying since the start of the Tour that anything can still happen on the final day. Fortunately, I'll start in the yellow jersey and I've already won two stages," she said</cite>. <cite index="25-11">She added: "I think tomorrow it's going to be a hard fight again, but I will do everything I have left because I don't want any regrets afterwards."</cite>

<cite index="22-1,22-3">With an eight-second lead on the line, the yellow jersey could easily change hands over four loops of the Col d'Eze</cite>.

clusters.leadHeadline: Fred Richard coasts to first national title at US gymnastics championships
clusters.summary: Fred Richard, 22, won his first national all-around title at the US gymnastics championships Saturday night, finishing two points clear of Shane Wiskus. The Paris bronze medalist's victory marks a rebound after a difficult 2025.
clusters.article:
Frederick Richard claimed his first national all-around title Saturday night at the US men's gymnastics championships, finishing two points ahead of runner-up Shane Wiskus in a dominant performance.

The 22-year-old's victory marks a significant rebound from a difficult 2025 and comes after his bronze medal at the Paris Olympics. Richard demonstrated the consistency and precision required to win a national championship, holding off strong competition throughout the competition.

His title comes as part of a broader reshaping of the US men's gymnastics landscape. Yul Moldauer won pommel horse gold, while Nedoroscik faltered in his event, signaling a shift in the hierarchy of American gymnasts.

Richard has stated his ambition to contend at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, making this national title a crucial step in that trajectory. The young gymnast's combination of technical skill and recent international experience positions him as a core piece of the US Olympic team planning for the home Games in Los Angeles.

clusters.leadHeadline: Everton's McNeil & Palace's Johnson poised for swap
clusters.summary: Everton and Crystal Palace are negotiating a player swap that would send winger Dwight McNeil to the Eagles in exchange for Wales international Brennan Johnson. The deal represents significant squad movement ahead of the transfer window.
clusters.article:
Everton and Crystal Palace are in active negotiations over a swap deal that would send Dwight McNeil from the Toffees to Palace while Brennan Johnson moves in the opposite direction to Goodison Park.

McNeil has been a consistent presence in Everton's lineup but has not reached the form the club hoped for when acquiring him. Johnson, a Wales international, represents Palace's attempt to inject attacking depth while allowing Everton to reshape its forward options.

Both players are in their mid-20s and bring Premier League experience. The swap structure suggests both clubs see value in a clean break rather than a straight cash transaction, though the exact financial arrangements were not disclosed.

If completed, the trade would mark meaningful movement for both sides as they finalize their squads ahead of the summer window. It also reflects the Premier League's increasing reliance on player-plus-cash arrangements to manage Financial Fair Play requirements and balance sheet considerations. The deal remains under discussion and is not yet finalized.

clusters.leadHeadline: Aggressive yet calm, Alexandrova pulls off upset win over No. 1 Sabalenka
clusters.summary: Ekaterina Alexandrova defeated top-seeded Aryna Sabalenka in a stunning upset at the Toronto tournament, keeping her composure against one of the world's hottest players. The result marks a significant scalp for Alexandrova.
clusters.article:
Ekaterina Alexandrova achieved a major upset Saturday night in Toronto, defeating world No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka in a tightly contested match that showcased Alexandrova's aggressive yet controlled approach.

Playing on a sticky, sweaty court, Alexandrova managed the conditions and Sabalenka's firepower to pull off the win. Sabalenka had entered the match as the tournament's top seed and one of the hottest players on the professional tour, making the result all the more impressive.

Alexandrova's win demonstrates that elite players can be beaten by disciplined opponents who refuse to engage in pace wars. Her aggressive yet calm demeanor throughout the match proved the decisive factor against Sabalenka's typically overwhelming power.

The upset has major implications for the tournament draw and signals potential vulnerabilities for Sabalenka despite her dominant form leading into Toronto. For Alexandrova, the victory provides significant momentum and ranking points heading into the remainder of the summer circuit.

clusters.leadHeadline: Vintage Scherzer, Guerrero help Blue Jays rally past Phillies
clusters.summary: Max Scherzer recorded his 3,516th career strikeout, 10th all-time, while Vladimir Guerrero Jr. showed signs of returning to form as the Blue Jays rallied past Philadelphia on Saturday. The win keeps Toronto competitive in a tight AL East race.
clusters.article:
Max Scherzer delivered a vintage performance Saturday, recording his 3,516th career strikeout to move into 10th place all-time, while Vladimir Guerrero Jr. showed encouraging signs of returning to his elite form as the Toronto Blue Jays rallied past the Philadelphia Phillies.

Scherzer's milestone strikeout came during a dominant outing that reminded observers why the 41-year-old remains one of baseball's most durable and effective arms. His precision and command throughout the game, even at an age when most pitchers are retired, underscored his extraordinary longevity.

Guerrero Jr.'s return from injury is the larger story for Toronto's future. The franchise cornerstone has been absent for stretches this season, and his performance against Philadelphia suggests he may be regaining the elite offensive consistency that makes the Blue Jays contenders in the AL East.

The victory keeps Toronto in the hunt in a competitive division and provides evidence that when both Scherzer and Guerrero Jr. perform at or near their peak levels, the Blue Jays have the offensive and pitching depth to compete with any team in baseball. The two victories over the Phillies put pressure on other AL East contenders.

clusters.leadHeadline: Senate Punts College Sports Bill to September
clusters.summary: The Senate has delayed action on a college sports bill, pushing the measure to September and extending the timeline for regulatory changes affecting NIL and athlete compensation. The bill faces a significant legislative hurdle before it can become law.
clusters.article:
The Senate has postponed consideration of a comprehensive college sports bill, moving the vote to September and ensuring that any regulatory changes affecting NIL deals and athlete compensation will not happen before the fall.

The delay gives advocacy groups, athletic departments, and legal experts additional time to weigh in on the proposal, which has become increasingly contentious as stakeholder positions have hardened. The bill's core provisions would establish federal guidelines for Name, Image, and Likeness deals and set standards for athlete compensation across Division I programs.

The postponement reflects the legislative complexity of regulating college sports without stripping athletes of compensation opportunities while also protecting institutional autonomy. Senators from states with major college programs have expressed concerns that overly restrictive rules could disadvantage their schools in recruiting.

With the vote now scheduled for September, the bill faces a long path to final passage. Even if the Senate approves the measure, it would still need House approval and presidential signature, making enactment unlikely before the 2026-27 college football season. The delay gives the college sports landscape another few months to operate under current NIL rules without federal oversight.

clusters.leadHeadline: Engelbert, WNBA Teams to Discuss Transgender Eligibility Rules
clusters.summary: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert will meet with team leadership to discuss transgender player eligibility rules following comments by Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham. The league is preparing formal policy guidance.
clusters.article:
WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert has scheduled discussions with team ownership and leadership to address transgender player eligibility policies, a move prompted by recent public comments from Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham.

Cunningham's remarks triggered conversation across the league about inclusion standards and competitive fairness, prompting the commissioner's office to formalize the league's position on player eligibility. The meetings represent the WNBA's effort to establish clear, league-wide guidelines that all 12 teams will follow.

The discussions will involve input from players, team executives, and medical professionals to ensure any policy reflects both competitive integrity and inclusive principles. The WNBA has not previously issued formal guidance on transgender eligibility, leaving individual teams to interpret league rules.

The timing suggests the league wants to establish clear policy before the 2026-27 season begins, giving teams and players clarity on eligibility standards heading into training camps. Similar conversations have occurred across professional sports as leagues work to balance inclusion with operational and competitive standards.

sidebar.headline: Port Washington two wins from Little League World Series after taking first regional game
sidebar.article: Port Washington won its opening game in the Little League regional tournament and sits two victories away from advancing to the Little League World Series in Williamsport, Pennsylvania. The team will play Monday in the winners bracket at 1 p.m., with a win putting them into the Metro Region finals. Port's path to the national tournament remains clear, though they'll face stiff competition from other regional qualifiers. A loss would drop them to the elimination bracket but wouldn't end their tournament hopes. Port's young roster has shown the consistency required to advance through a crowded regional, suggesting they have the pitching depth and batting to make a run.

sidebar.headline: Fantasy football rankings 2026: Sleepers, breakouts, busts via model that nailed Daniel Jones big year
sidebar.article: CBS Sports' advanced computer model has released its 2026 fantasy football rankings after simulating the upcoming NFL season 10,000 times. The model, which correctly predicted Daniel Jones' breakout 2025 performance, identifies sleepers, breakouts, and potential busts for fantasy drafters preparing for next season. The rankings incorporate expected workload, opportunity, and matchup data across all 32 teams. Owners should pay close attention to the model's sleeper selections in middle rounds, where value is often concentrated. The rankings will be updated throughout the offseason as trades and free agency reshape roster compositions.

sidebar.headline: Which college football teams can go undefeated in 2026?
sidebar.article: CBS Sports has identified 10 college football teams with the talent, coaching, and schedule favorability to complete an undefeated 2026 season. The analysis factors in returning talent, off-season recruiting, and strength of schedule to determine which programs have the pieces to go wire-to-wire. Teams with elite quarterbacks, experienced defensive secondaries, and favorable non-conference schedules appear most likely to avoid a loss. The 2025 season produced no undefeated teams despite several contenders, making any undefeated run in 2026 a significant achievement. Injuries, coaching changes, and mid-season losses have typically derailed previous attempts at perfection.

sidebar.headline: Mavs Owner Patrick Dumont Hits Back at Mark Cuban in Arena Fight
sidebar.article: Dallas Mavericks owner Patrick Dumont has responded to Mark Cuban's public disputes, with both parties claiming the other violated contractual agreements. Dumont says Cuban is required to arbitrate any disputes privately rather than through public statements. The arena ownership dispute centers on the American Airlines Center and the operational control of the franchise. The two have been in conflict over management decisions and long-term strategic direction. Any arbitration will occur behind closed doors, keeping the specifics of their disagreement away from public scrutiny and potentially limiting further escalation.

sidebar.headline: Brazilian top-flight club wear name of English fan with MND on shirts
sidebar.article: Coritiba, a Brazilian top-flight club, wore the name of an English Norwich fan on their shirts to raise awareness of motor neurone disease. The gesture honored the fan's battle with MND while using the platform of professional football to highlight the neurological condition. Coritiba's decision reflects growing efforts by clubs worldwide to use match days for social causes. The initiative brought MND awareness to millions of viewers across Brazil and internationally. The club plans to continue raising awareness throughout the season.

sidebar.article: CBS Sports' computer model has released predictions and prop bets for the Iowa Corn 350 NASCAR race, featuring picks from a model with a strong track record of accuracy. The analysis covers driver matchups, pit strategy implications, and track-specific variables that typically affect Iowa races. Historical data and current driver form factor into the model's recommendations. Bettors should focus on the model's top prop selections rather than overall race winner picks, where value concentrates in longer odds. predictions.statement: The Senate's college sports bill passes final congressional approval by December 2026.
predictions.rationale: A September vote gives the bill momentum, but it still needs House passage and faces lobbying from athletic departments and conferences. Lame-duck sessions rarely prioritize sports regulation over other legislative items.

The line was artificially suppressed after his Game 1 outlier (2 assists on 31 shot attempts in Finals survival mode), which is not representative of his playoff baseline. The market overreacted to a non-repeatable game and has not adjusted back to his 6.6 APG average despite the Finals being a series where Knicks role players will see significant minutes, increasing Brunson's playmaking opportunities.
